articles.title: Introducing Search for Agents
articles.excerpt: AI Search , our service that indexes your content and lets you add search to any application or agent without having to build an entire retrieval infrastructure, has supported adding your website as a data source for a while now, automatically crawling, converting and indexing its pages. Still, setting up an AI Search instance for your website requires manually creating and configuring it initially, and then doing all the integration work to get the search endpoints available from your domain and to make sure that agents know where to find the index and know how to use it. Today we're introducing Search for Agents , which puts that setup behind a toggle in your Cloudflare dashboard. Turn it on for your zone, and our service will create your AI Search instance, start indexing your content, and make search discoverable and available from your own domain. How it works The idea follows naturally from Markdown for Agents , where Cloudflare's network converts any HTML page to Markdown in real time for enabled zones using content negotiation headers. Similarly, Search for Agents leverages the power of AI Search by automatically creating an index for your zone and exposing APIs that any AI agent can discover and use to search your website, under your domain, all done at the network level. You can enable Search for Agents using the API, or by going to the dashboard in your zone page, under Quick Actions : Search for Agents is available to all customers, including Free (with limits ). Once it’s enabled, Cloudflare will automatically create an AI Search instance, start crawling and indexing the content in your zone. Refer to our developer documentation to understand how the crawling process works. You can access your instance directly from this page, or by going to directly to your account’s AI > AI Search instances view: The AI Search instance for your zone is created with default settings, but you can enable reranking or change configuration options like cache sett
articles.summary: Cloudflare simplifie l'ajout de recherche IA sur un site via un toggle, rendant les données indexables et accessibles aux agents.

articles.title: AWS IAM extends trusted identity propagation to IAM federation and IAM Roles Anywhere, and simplifies it in IAM Identity Center
articles.excerpt: Trusted identity propagation (TIP) carries the identity of a human user or workload with requests to supported AWS Services. Customers can use that identity in IAM policy conditions for access control and to identify the originating human user or workload in AWS CloudTrail. AWS is expanding TIP to AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) federation and IAM Roles Anywhere , while simplifying the existing TIP experience in AWS IAM Identity Center. In addition, IAM outbound identity federation now enables customers to request an AWS-signed JSON Web Token (JWT) that includes identity information from TIP sessions, allowing external services to identify the human user or workload that originated the request. With TIP for IAM federation, customers can map the human or workload identity, along with optional runtime claims such as a risk score or a CI/CD workflow name, from the SAML assertion or OIDC token used for federation to the role session. IAM Roles Anywhere extends TIP to identities sourced from X.509 certificates. For IAM Identity Center, which supports workforce identities, the simplified experience adds the username, an identifier provided by your identity source, alongside the user ID that IAM Identity Center generates, and carries this information uniformly whether users access applications or AWS accounts. Across all supported paths, TIP preserves identity information as requests move between IAM roles and AWS services without requiring per-role trust policy updates. TIP for IAM federation, IAM Roles Anywhere, IAM outbound identity federation, and the simplified IAM Identity Center experience are available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. To get started, see the Trusted Identity Propagation for IAM documentation , Trusted Identity Propagation in IAM Identity Center documentation , and the TIP launch blog .
articles.summary: AWS étend la propagation d'identité de confiance à IAM federation et Roles Anywhere, simplifiant IAM Identity Center pour une traçabilité unifiée.

articles.title: Take on complex coding changes with Gemini 4 Neon on GitLab
articles.excerpt: Google's Gemini 4 Neon is now available on GitLab Duo Agent Platform , offering engineers a versatile model for agentic work, with particular strength in coding. Gemini 4 Neon is the latest addition to a growing Gemini 4 lineup on GitLab Duo Agent Platform, joining Argon, Hydrogen, and Carbon. Each model brings its own balance of speed, reasoning, and cost, giving your team a broad selection of Gemini models to power everything from quick fixes to large, cross-codebase refactors. Neon handles the mix of tasks an agent takes on in a day, such as planning an issue, reading a long spec, answering questions about a codebase in Agentic Chat, and then making the change. It performs best on agentic coding, where an agent has to read, run, and edit its way to a change ready for review. Carry complex coding work through to a merge request On GitLab's software engineering benchmark, Neon completed 100% of tasks, returning a merge request each time, and resolved 76.7% of those tasks, with changes that passed the benchmark's tests. Neon executes well on tasks that take many steps and require judgement before they're ready for review. That makes this model a good choice for changes that reach across a codebase, like a feature that needs a new option carried from configuration through to the UI, a bug whose fix spans several modules, or a refactor that has to land in every package that depends on it. Your engineers can hand off that work and come back to a merge request they can review. Choose your model across the Gemini 4 lineup Across the Gemini 4 models in GitLab, your team has a range of strengths to draw on. Neon balances reasoning and efficiency, and does especially well carrying out coding changes that touch multiple files. articles.title: Amazon Bedrock adds bedrock-runtime endpoint support for OpenAI Daybreak Red in AWS GovCloud (US)
articles.excerpt: Eligible customers can now access OpenAI’s specialized cybersecurity models Daybreak Red: GPT-5.6 Cyber through the bedrock-runtime endpoint on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US). Daybreak Red is designed for advanced, authorized tasks such as vulnerability research, exploit reproduction, and mitigation development. For these tasks, a lower refusal threshold, matched by stronger identity verification, monitoring, and access controls, improves the speed and depth of an investigation. Your inference data is not used for model training, and you are not required to opt in to sharing your data with OpenAI. On the bedrock-runtime endpoint, the model is available through the US Gov Geo cross-Region inference (CRIS) profile. Access to the model requires enrollment in Daybreak access from OpenAI. To enroll, contact OpenAI or reach out to your AWS account team for guidance on eligibility. Once approved, work with your account team to request access on AWS. For regional availability through the bedrock-mantle endpoint and more information, view the documentation.
articles.summary: AWS GovCloud (US) propose désormais Daybreak Red d'OpenAI via Bedrock pour la cybersécurité, avec contrôles renforcés et données protégées.

articles.title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless is now available in the Africa (Cape Town) Region
articles.excerpt: Starting today, the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless is available in the AWS Africa (Cape Town) Region. Customers can now use a fully managed search, vector and analytics engine that provisions resources in seconds, auto scales instantly to meet changing demand, and scales to zero when idle, so customers only pay for the compute they use. With this launch, customers in the Africa (Cape Town) Region can run agentic AI, search, and observability workloads without provisioning or managing clusters. Compute is fully separated from storage, which lets customers scale compute independently to reduce costs during low-traffic periods while remaining ready for traffic spikes. With scale-to-zero and pay-per-usage pricing, customers can save up to 60% compared to provisioning OpenSearch clusters for peak loads. To learn more, see the OpenSearch Serverless documentation and pricing page . For the full list of AWS Regions where OpenSearch Serverless is available, see the Regional Services List.
articles.summary: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless est désormais disponible en Afrique du Sud (Le Cap), offrant un moteur de recherche et d'analytique serverless et auto-scalable.

articles.title: AWS CloudFormation makes resource coverage comprehensive with 206 new types
articles.excerpt: AWS CloudFormation now supports 206 additional resource types across 88 services, including Amazon SageMaker Hub, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore PolicyEngine, and Amazon EC2 Snapshot. This closes key gaps in CloudFormation coverage and helps customers to standardize on safe and scalable infrastructure management workflows. The launch utilized a new AI-driven internal framework to collapse the costs of onboarding resource types to CloudFormation, setting up CloudFormation for continued coverage expansion. AWS Cloud Control API supports all new resource types that CloudFormation supports. Additionally, Cloud Control API now supports 224 read-only resource types across 99 services, making it easier to find and inspect existing AWS resources. CloudFormation resource coverage is available across all AWS Regions where the underlying service is available. To learn more, visit the AWS resource and property types reference , the Cloud Control API resource list , and the AWS CloudFormation User Guide .
articles.summary: AWS CloudFormation ajoute 206 nouveaux types de ressources, couvrant 88 services dont SageMaker et Bedrock, pour une gestion d'infrastructure plus complète.
